Analytic Hierarchy Process Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch67.R
centrality_ahp.Rd

Analytic hierarchy process centrality (AHP; Bian et al. 2017) adds the shares a node holds of the degree, the betweenness and the closeness of the network, each discounted by the share of nodes where that measure is not zero: $$AHP(i) = \sum_{j=1}^{3} w_j \frac{N^+_j}{N} \frac{x_{ij}}{\sum_l x_{lj}},$$ with \(x_{i1}\) the degree, \(x_{i2}\) the betweenness, \(x_{i3}\) the closeness (the reciprocal of the sum of distances), \(N^+_j\) the number of nodes where \(x_{lj} > 0\) and \(w\) the weights.

Usage

centrality_ahp(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses ahp_weights (the weights of degree, betweenness and closeness, default one third each).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. This is the computation of the source's worked example: for each measure a matrix of the ratios between the nodes, with 0 where either value is 0, whose priority vector is the column-normalised row mean, which gives the formula above. The source's equation (10) names the principal eigenvector instead, which its printed numbers do not follow. The source derives the weights from a simulated spreading process whose printed values cannot be regenerated; evaluated as the source evaluates it, its weight rule gives weights within a few thousandths of one third for any realistic spreading count. ahp_weights holds the weights of degree, betweenness and closeness, one third each by default, and uses them as given. Each share does not depend on the scale of its measure, so the normalisation of the betweenness does not matter. Closeness has no value on a disconnected or a one-node network; the measure then warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA. With ahp_weights = c(1, 0, 0) and c(0, 0, 1) the implementation reproduces the 20 shares the source prints for the degree and the closeness of the kite network, and with the source's weights its ranking of Table 3. The betweenness matrix the source prints is not that of the kite (two nodes that are symmetric in the kite differ in it), so its betweenness shares and final scores are not reproduced; the final scores differ by at most 0.013. The score ranks nodes much like centrality_topsis (Kendall correlation 0.96 to 0.995 on four test networks, mean 0.975) and centrality_relative_entropy (mean 0.94, 0.992 on one network). A weight that is negative or not finite, or a ahp_weights that is not three numbers, raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Bian, T., Hu, J. and Deng, Y. (2017). Identifying influential nodes in complex networks based on AHP. Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications, 479, 422-436. doi:10.1016/j.physa.2017.02.085 .

See also

centrality_topsis, centrality_degree, centrality_betweenness, centrality_closeness, centrality.

Examples

centrality_ahp(to_undirected(regulation_net))
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#> 0.08896395 0.11664510 0.13555447 0.12744757 0.10316148 0.08958123 0.06660409 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#> 0.08340839 0.10738584 0.08124790 
centrality_ahp(to_undirected(regulation_net), ahp_weights = c(0.5, 0.25, 0.25))
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#> 0.08987111 0.11526160 0.13407326 0.12336345 0.10051926 0.09033407 0.06847158 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#> 0.08570444 0.10831716 0.08408407
